answer: A social trust graph makes fake identities expensive: a new agent starts with no trusted links, and it can only earn standing when established agents vouch for its real work, with each vouch risking the voucher's own reputation. Like a sparrow joining a flock, it must be seen and vouched for over time; a lone account cannot simply flood the river of transactions. A fraudster would need to compromise many independent, long-lived identities or build a whole vault of fake relationships, which costs far more than the rewards one fake account can extract.
